lead.headline: Democrats win both houses of Congress in a 'blue wave', taking Senate seats in Kansas, Texas and South Carolina
lead.byline: THE GUARDIAN · THE TIMES OF INDIA · THE HINDU · 4 NOV
lead.short: Democrats won control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in Tuesday's midterm elections, flipping seven Senate seats and more than two dozen House seats in a rebuke to Donald Trump. They took historically Republican Senate seats in Iowa, Kansas, North Carolina, South Carolina and Texas. Trump said he would have won had he been on the ballot.

why.text: A Democratic Congress can block Trump's agenda for his last two years, including on tariffs and the Iran war, both of which hit India's trade and fuel bills.

more: Adam Hamilton became the first Democrat to win a Senate seat in Kansas in 94 years, and James Talarico the first Democrat to win in Texas since 1988. In South Carolina, Annie Andrews beat Darline Graham, the late Lindsey Graham's sister and a Trump ally. In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed became the first Muslim US senator after a campaign in which Trump called him a "jihadist". In Ohio, Democrat Amy Acton beat Vivek Ramaswamy for governor.

Nearly nine in 10 voters called the cost of living a major factor, and nearly two-thirds blamed Trump for high prices, exit polls by SSRS found. Elon Musk, who gave nearly half a billion dollars to Republican efforts, joked: "Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn't work this time." Indian-American Pia Dandiya won a Florida House seat.

facts.House: Democratic majority; more than two dozen seats flipped

update.new: The results: Democrats win both houses.
update.front: Trump has lost Congress, which changes what he can do for the rest of his term.

seconds.headline: Arshdeep's four wickets bowl New Zealand out for 185 in Auckland, and Kohli becomes the first to 13,000 ODI runs at No. 3
seconds.short: India bowled New Zealand out for 185 in 40.2 overs in the first ODI at Eden Park on Wednesday, with Arshdeep Singh taking four wickets, Gurnoor Brar three and Anshul Kamboj two. Rain then stopped play with India on 64 for one after 12 overs. Virat Kohli became the first batter to score 13,000 ODI runs at No. 3.

why.text: It is India's first ODI with Kohli and Rohit back in the side, and the start of their build-up to next year's World Cup.

more: Captain Shubman Gill chose to bowl and picked four specialist fast bowlers with 29 international matches between them, leaving out Mohammed Siraj. Kohli dived to his right at second slip for a low catch off Kamboj to remove Nathan Smith and leave New Zealand 115 for seven, and Rohit Sharma ran out Daryl Mitchell with an underarm throw from mid-wicket.

Kohli now has 13,000 runs at No. 3 at an average of 61.61, ahead of Ricky Ponting's 12,662; only Sachin Tendulkar has scored more at a single position, with 13,685 as an opener. New Zealand were without Devon Conway, concussed in training. The second ODI is in Wellington on Saturday.

update.new: The first ODI: New Zealand 185 all out; rain with India 64 for one.
update.front: India's ODI side with Kohli and Rohit back is in a winning position at the cut.

seconds.headline: The Supreme Court says laws penalising people for having more than two children have lost their relevance as fertility falls
seconds.short: The Supreme Court held on Wednesday that laws punishing people for having more than two children have lost their relevance because India's fertility rate has fallen. "The foundation of such laws, that is the fear of overpopulation, has crumbled," said a bench headed by Justice P.S. Narasimha. It referred the legal question to a larger bench.

why.text: Several states bar people with more than two children from contesting local elections, and this ruling begins the end of those rules.

more: The court noted that India's total fertility rate has fallen from 3 to 1.9, below the replacement rate of 2.1. Even though the population is not yet shrinking, a rate below replacement will soon mean an older population with a smaller share of working-age people. "If we fail to take note of such demographic changes, India will face serious consequences," Justice Narasimha wrote.

The case concerned laws that make the two-child norm a condition for contesting elections. "Allowing such laws to stand excludes an entire class of citizens from political" life, the court said. Whether people must keep to the norm or face penalties is now for a larger bench to decide.

facts.next: question referred to a larger bench

seconds.headline: Spain's transport minister Óscar Puente resigns six days after the train crash that killed 69
seconds.short: Spain's transport minister Óscar Puente resigned on Tuesday, six days after a high-speed train collision south of Madrid killed 69 people, the country's second major rail disaster this year. "A transport minister in a country like Spain cannot remain in office after two accidents of this seriousness in less than a year," he said after hours of questioning by lawmakers.

why.text: It is the first resignation over a crash that has shaken confidence in one of Europe's biggest high-speed networks, weeks before a snap election.

more: The collision on 28 October happened after a communication system essential to safety on the Madrid-Seville line failed. Controllers in Madrid took over and allowed a state-run Renfe train to proceed although a train run by the private company Iryo had stopped ahead. "There was a red signal prohibiting movement, yet the train was authorised to proceed," Puente said last week.

In January two high-speed trains collided near Adamuz, further south on the same route, killing 46. Puente said he decided to quit straight after the latest crash but kept it private. Before resigning, he announced safety measures including a faster rollout of the European Rail Traffic Management System.

facts.cause: train authorised past a red signal

update.front: A minister has resigned over the disaster, the first political cost of the crash.

seconds.headline: Canva cuts 1,271 jobs, about 22% of its staff, as its chief executive calls this its 'hardest year yet'
seconds.short: Canva, the Australian design software company, is restructuring in a way that affects 1,271 employees, about 22% of its global workforce, co-founder and chief executive Melanie Perkins told staff. She said growth had slowed for the first time in a decade and called it the hardest moment in the company's 13-year history. Some staff will leave.

why.text: Canva is one of the best-known design tools in Indian offices and classrooms, and its cuts show how AI rivals are squeezing software makers.

more: "This has been our hardest year yet," Perkins wrote in a long message later published on the company's website. She said Canva had looked at smaller changes before deciding they would not prepare the business for the long term, and that it needed to "refound Canva" by going back to smaller, empowered teams with more ownership.

The company works across 37 countries. Some employees will be asked to move to central hubs or take new roles rather than leave, and Canva has set out a support package for those who go. Perkins apologised to those affected for the pain and disruption.

briefs.headline: Delhi brings in Stage II of its pollution plan, with extra Metro trips and staggered office hours, as the AQI stays above 300
briefs.text: Delhi Metro has added 20 weekday trips and parking charges are higher. The air has worsened after an unusually clean October as winds slowed and crop burning rose in Punjab and Haryana, days before Diwali.

update.new: Stage II curbs are in force.

stories.headline: Michigan elects Abdul El-Sayed, a progressive doctor, as the first Muslim US senator
stories.short: Abdul El-Sayed, a doctor and progressive Democrat, won Michigan's Senate race against Trump-backed Republican Mike Rogers, becoming the first Muslim US senator. His opponents, including Donald Trump, ran a campaign that often pointed to his name and faith; Trump called him a "jihadist". El-Sayed, 42, declared victory early on Wednesday in Detroit.

why.text: His win, after a campaign full of attacks on his faith, is the clearest sign of how far the ground has shifted against Trump.

more: "You took a chance on the unlikeliest of candidates," El-Sayed told supporters. "You welcomed me in your homes, your churches, your synagogues." He said his opponents chose division because they had no answer to the cost of gas and groceries. "They want an America that is too small for some of us. We know that America is big enough for all of us."

A former Wayne County health director, he beat the establishment favourite Haley Stevens in the primary; on Sunday she endorsed Rogers. He backs universal healthcare under Medicare for All and an end to US military aid for Israel. Rogers had lost the 2024 Senate race to Elissa Slotkin by about 0.3 points. El-Sayed succeeds the retiring Democrat Gary Peters.

stories.headline: Apple lets any app plug into Siri AI in the iOS 27.3 beta, and gives Siri new actions across its own apps
stories.short: Apple began testing iOS 27.3 with developers on Tuesday, its biggest update since iOS 27 launched in September. A Developer Preview lets any app bring its content and actions into Siri AI through App Intents, and Siri can now complete more complex tasks across 15 of Apple's own apps. Siri AI also adds Traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish and Norwegian.

why.text: Opening Siri to every app is Apple's answer to AI assistants that can act across a phone, and Indian app makers can build for it now.

more: In Mail, Siri can unsubscribe you from mailing lists and undo recently sent messages; in Safari it can clear browsing history, manage tabs and save articles to the Reading List; in Files it can organise content and delete files you have not opened for a set time. Users can ask Siri what it can do in each app.

Safari also gets a vertical tabs layout and an adaptive dark mode for websites without one. The release is the same one in which Apple plans to bring Alibaba's Qwen into Apple Intelligence for users in China, with wider availability in December.

briefs.text: Gemini and its classroom tools will be off for K-12 student accounts until administrators switch them on. "Search and AI are deeply integrated," said Chris Phillips, Google's vice-president for education.

briefs.headline: NASA's Swift telescope is due to fall to Earth today after a $30m robotic rescue mission failed
briefs.text: The $30m LINK rescue spacecraft failed because of control problems. Launched in 2004 for a two-year mission, it studied gamma-ray bursts for two decades before solar activity dragged its orbit down.

update.new: Re-entry day; details of the failed rescue.

briefs.headline: CERN physicists find the first evidence of a particle decay so rare it happens once in 10 billion, after 42 years of searching
briefs.text: The result from the upgraded LHCb experiment gives a new test of the Standard Model. Physicists say it opens a window on the 'Zeptoverse', distances of a billionth of a trillionth of a metre.

briefs.text: It has a more realistic look, a jump button, sprinting and full voice acting. Nintendo is also selling a special Triforce edition of the Switch 2.

update.new: The Ocarina of Time remake is out tomorrow.

stories.headline: BMTC's minimum bus fare rises from ₹6 to ₹10 from tonight, and the airport bus goes up to ₹425
stories.byline: THE TIMES OF INDIA · PTI · 4 NOV
stories.short: Bus fares on Karnataka's four state-run transport corporations rise from Wednesday midnight, Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh announced. In Bengaluru, BMTC's minimum fare goes from ₹6 to ₹10 and its maximum from ₹35 to ₹45. AC Vajra buses rise to a top fare of ₹90, and Vayu Vajra airport services to up to ₹425, from ₹405.

why.text: Most of Bengaluru's commuters ride BMTC, and this is the fare they pay every day from Thursday.

more: Suresh blamed the rise in diesel prices, and said Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra had raised their bus fares too. The increase on KSRTC services is capped at ₹9, while fares for luxury services such as Rajahamsa and AC buses were set with competitors' prices in mind, he said.

City bus fares rise by up to ₹10 in all, and the new fares apply from Thursday. Women continue to travel free on non-luxury government buses under the state's Shakti scheme, so the increase falls on men and on women using AC and luxury services. The maximum AC Vajra fare goes from ₹75 to ₹90.
